x: The Abhidhamma Pitaka is the philosophical and analytical exposition of the Dhamma. The Sutta Pitaka holds the Buddha's discourses, the Vinaya Pitaka the monastic rules, and there is no "Sangha Pitaka".
t: Discriminate the content of each Pitaka.

x: The Tripitaka is Vinaya + Sutta + Abhidhamma Pitaka. Vibhanga, Dhammasangani and Patthana are books inside the Abhidhamma Pitaka, not Pitakas themselves.
t: Separate the three Pitakas from the books within them.

x: Both are true: the Abhidhamma Pitaka is the analytical exposition of the Dhamma, and Dhammasangani is its first of seven books.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Only I is correct: Patthana is the seventh book of the Abhidhamma Pitaka. II and III are false because Sutta and Vinaya are separate Pitakas, not books of the Abhidhamma.
t: Separate Pitaka names from Abhidhamma book names.

x: Vinaya Pitaka holds the rules of the Sangha, Sutta Pitaka the Buddha's discourses, Abhidhamma Pitaka the analytical exposition of Dhamma, and Tripitaka means the three together, giving a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Recall the content of each Pitaka.

x: The Abhidhamma Pitaka has seven books, from Dhammasangani (first) to Patthana (seventh).
t: Recall the number of Abhidhamma books.

x: The order is Dhammasangani, Vibhanga, Dhatukatha, Puggalapannatti, Kathavatthu, Yamaka and Patthana. The other options swap Vibhanga, Dhatukatha, Kathavatthu or Yamaka out of place.
t: Fix the first and last books, then check the middle order.

x: Sanchi is in Raisen (MP), Bharhut in Satna (MP), Amaravati on the right bank of the Krishna in Andhra Pradesh, and Dhamek at Sarnath near Varanasi, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the location of each stupa.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Dhamek's original structure goes back to Ashoka, while its present form was rebuilt in the Gupta period. The Ashokan origin does not cause the Gupta form.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: All three are correct: Sanchi is linked with Ashoka, Bharhut is a classic example of Shunga art, and Colin Mackenzie traced the Amaravati Stupa in 1797.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Alexander Cunningham discovered Bharhut in 1873, and Bharhut separately represents Shunga architecture. Its style is not why he found it.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Three are associated with Ashoka: Sanchi Stupa, the original Dhamek Stupa and the Kanakamuni Stupa, which he enlarged. Ranabhar (Ramabhar) Stupa at Kushinagar was built by the Mallas over the Buddha's cremation site.
t: Check the Ashokan link of each stupa.

x: Sanchi is rated the finest stupa architecturally, Bharhut was discovered by Cunningham, Amaravati was traced by Mackenzie in 1797, and Dhamek's present form is Gupta, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the key association of each stupa.

x: I and II are correct: Kanakamuni Stupa is at Niglihawa in Nepal, and Ranabhar Stupa is at Kushinagar. III is false because Dhamek Stupa is at Sarnath, Varanasi; Satna is the district of Bharhut.
t: Check the location in each statement.

x: All three are correct: Stupa No. 1 is the Great Stupa, Stupa No. 2 holds relics of monks of the Ashokan missionary era (called Dhamma Mahamatras here), and Stupa No. 3 holds relics of Sariputra and Mudgalayana.
t: Recall what each numbered Sanchi stupa contains.

x: Three are at Sanchi: Stupa Nos. 1, 2 and 3. The Kanakamuni Stupa is at Niglihawa in Nepal.
t: Check the location of each stupa.

x: The item is doubtful: the key marks A, but relics of Sariputta and Moggallana (Sariputra and Mudgalayana) really were found at Sanchi, in Stupa No. 3. B and D are also true, so no option is clearly incorrect.
t: Check each statement against the find-spot.

x: A is true: a relic casket with gold items was found at Bhattiprolu. B is keyed false because monastery and stupa remains are matched with Devnimori, Gujarat, and Sopara with the eight Ashokan Dharmachakras. The item is doubtful, as Sopara also has a known stupa.
t: Check each find-spot separately.

x: I and II are correct: the "Sakiyanam" casket came from Piprahwa and a bone relic casket from Dharmarajika, Taxila. III is false because the gold relic casket was found at Bhattiprolu, not Sopara.
t: Check the find-spot in each statement.

x: Remains linked with Ashoka's Dhamma Mahamatras are at Sanchi Stupa 2, Chandragupta's palace at Kumrahar, the Pataliputra city wall at Bulandibagh, and the "Sakiyanam" casket at Piprahwa, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the site of each find.

x: Sariputra and Mudgalayana go with Sanchi Stupa 3, Sariputta and Moggallana with Sanchi, the bone relic casket with Dharmarajika, Taxila, and the gold casket with Bhattiprolu, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i.
t: Match the unique pairs first, then the Sanchi pair.

x: The eight Ashokan Dharmachakras go with Sopara, monastery and stupa remains with Devnimori, Gujarat, Chandragupta's palace with Kumrahar and the city wall with Bulandibagh, giving a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Recall the site of each find.

x: All four yielded relics: Piprahwa (the Buddha's relics), Sanchi (Sariputta and Moggallana), Dharmarajika at Taxila (bone relic casket) and Bhattiprolu (relic casket).
t: Check each site for a relic find.

x: Both are true: Sanchi is linked with three finds (Stupa 2 relics, Stupa 3 relics of Sariputra and Mudgalayana, and the Sariputta-Moggallana relics), and the Pataliputra finds are the palace at Kumrahar and the city wall at Bulandibagh.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: All four refer to a stupa: Sanchi Stupa 2, Sanchi Stupa 3, Piprahwa Stupa and the stupa remains at Devnimori.
t: Check each entry for the word stupa.

x: At the First Council at Rajagriha, Mahakassapa presided, Ananda recited the Buddha's teachings (Sutta) and Upali recited the Vinaya, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-i.
t: Recall each monk's role at the First Council.

x: Both are true and R explains A: Nagasena is linked with King Menander (Milinda) through their dialogue recorded in the Milindapanha.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Nagarjuna, traditionally placed in Kanishka's era, founded the Madhyamika school based on Shunyata (emptiness). Vasubandhu was Yogachara, Dignaga a logician, and Nagasena debated Menander.
t: Link each scholar to his school.

x: Nagarjuna founded Madhyamika and Shunyata, Aryadeva was his disciple, Vasubandhu belongs to Yogachara, and Dignaga was a major Buddhist logician, giving a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.
t: Recall each scholar's school or role.

x: Vasubandhu was a leading philosopher of the Yogachara tradition. Madhyamika belongs to Nagarjuna, and Theravada to scholars such as Buddhaghosa.
t: Discriminate Yogachara from Madhyamika.

x: Buddhaghosa, the Theravada commentator, wrote the Visuddhimagga. Nagarjuna was Madhyamika, Vasubandhu Yogachara, and Dharmakirti a logician.
t: Recall the author of each text.

x: I and II are correct: Dignaga was a major Buddhist logician and Dharmakirti developed his tradition. III is false because Aryadeva was Nagarjuna's disciple in Madhyamika; Yogachara belongs to Vasubandhu.
t: Check each scholar's school separately.

x: Both are true: Fa-Hien visited Gupta India under Chandragupta II, and Hiuen-Tsang was a Chinese monk-pilgrim during Harsha's reign.
t: Recall the ruler linked to each pilgrim.

x: Fa-Hien goes with Gupta India, Hiuen-Tsang with Harsha, and I-Tsing with 7th-century India, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-i.
t: Recall the period of each Chinese traveller.

x: I-Tsing gave a detailed account of monastic life in 7th-century India, notably at Nalanda. Fa-Hien came in the Gupta age, Hiuen-Tsang under Harsha, and Nagasena was not Chinese.
t: Discriminate the three Chinese travellers.

x: Three are correct: Mahakassapa presided over the First Council, Buddhaghosa wrote Visuddhimagga, and Vasubandhu was Yogachara. IV is wrong because Upali recited the Vinaya; Dharmakirti was a logician.
t: Check each pair separately.

x: Menander, the Indo-Greek king, is called Milinda in Pali texts. His dialogue with Nagasena is the Milindapanha.
t: Link the king's name to the text title.

x: Three were Chinese monk-pilgrims: Fa-Hien, Hiuen-Tsang and I-Tsing. Nagarjuna was an Indian Buddhist philosopher, founder of Madhyamika.
t: Check the nationality of each person.

x: Both are true: Mahakassapa is the Pali form of Mahakasyapa, and Aryadeva was a Buddhist philosopher and disciple of Nagarjuna.
t: Check each statement separately.
